prompts.prompt: Design a URL shortener like bit.ly: 100M URLs/month, 10:1 read:write ratio.
sample_structure: Requirements: functional (shorten, redirect, custom aliases, expiry) + non-functional (latency, availability, scale numbers)
ID generation: hash+collision vs base62 counter vs KGS; trade-offs
Storage: schema, sharding, caching hot URLs
Deep dive: pick one hard part (e.g., handling custom aliases at scale) and go deep
prompts.what_good_looks_like: Starts with clarifying questions and scale math; makes explicit trade-offs; goes deep on one component rather than shallow on all.

prompts.prompt: Design a feed ranking system for a social app: 500M DAU, 100ms p99 latency budget.
sample_structure: Clarify objective: what does 'good ranking' mean? North-star + guardrails
Candidate generation: retrieval from follow graph, two-tower embeddings
Ranking: features (user, item, context), model choice, training objective
Serving: feature store, online inference, caching, fallback
Experimentation: how you A/B test a ranker (interleaving vs A/B)
Feedback loops: label delay, position bias, exploration
Monitoring: prediction drift, business metric dashboards, rollback plan
prompts.what_good_looks_like: Thinks in loops (train/serve/monitor/retrain); names label delay and position bias; has a rollout plan.

prompts.prompt: Design a distributed rate limiter: 1M requests/sec across regions.
sample_structure: Requirements: per-user vs per-API-key limits, burst vs sustained
Algorithms: token bucket vs sliding window vs fixed window; trade-offs
Distributed state: Redis, sticky routing, approximate counting
Edge cases: clock skew, fail-open vs fail-closed
prompts.what_good_looks_like: Compares algorithms with trade-offs; addresses distributed-state consistency explicitly.

checks: Named components and data flow end to end
Chose specific technologies with reasons, not buzzwords
Compared at least two options for key decisions
Named what they give up with each choice
Went deep on the hardest component
Drew/whiteboarded the system as they talked
